text:
Alex: noticing a p95 decode latency spike on canary right after the merge of PR #4893. baseline p95 ~42ms -> 78ms on shortseq workloads.
Tina: ack, saw CI perf alert too. Jenkins job perf/shortseq throughput -18% on head. link: https://ci.redwood/jenkins/job/perf/4893
Pranav: any obvious perf traces? I can run perf/heap profile on the failing canary.
Alex: copied flamegraph from a repro run (local docker reproduce):\n```
# decode tail flamegraph snippet
fast_attn_kernel  60%
fallback_attn_kernel 25%
kv-copy 10%
other 5%
```\nLooks like the selector flipped to fallback_attn_kernel for many requests.
Tina: that matches the kernel-selector logs i pulled. Selector recorded entropy_score > 0.7 on many minibatches and chose fallback despite short sequence length. snippet:\n```
[selector] seq=16 entropy=0.72 chosen=fallback_attn reason="entropy>0.7"
```
Pranav: hmm, PR #4893 changed the entropy heuristic threshold to 0.7 and also modified prefetch warm-start behavior (PR description: "avoid pathological attn for degenerate patterns")
Hamid: could be an interaction: the new warm-start path leaves KV-cache refs uninitialized for the first token which spikes entropy calc and forces fallback kernel until KV warm-up finishes.
Alex: repro script: `python tools/repro_perf.py --model small --seq 16 --batch 8 --tokens 512 --warm-start` shows consistent p95 bump. attaching short log output:\n```
p50  12ms
p95  78ms
throughput  tokens/s  4200 (baseline  5100)
```\nci-bench-bot: perf regression detected: job perf/shortseq @3629989920 diff -17.8% throughput. regression surface: decode-path+kernel-selector. See report: https://ci.redwood/reports/3629989920
Tina: can we bisect to the exact commit in PR? Pranav, can you run `git bisect` on the PR branch with the perf harness? If not, we may consider an immediate revert of the selector change.
Pranav: started a quick bisect on a pinned image. Preliminary result: the change that toggles `entropy_threshold` + the warm-start KV init commit together cause the flip. isolating now.
Hamid: quick mitigation idea: if seq_len <= 32 and batch_size <= 16 force kernel_selector to prefer fast_attn unless explicit mismatch. cheap guard to avoid mass fallback.
Alex: that guard reduced p95 from 78ms -> 46ms in local test. good stopgap.
Tina: ops: should we hold the rollout? current canary qps ~5% of traffic, we should pause until we have a fix or revert. @OpsBot can you hold the rollout? :pause_button:
OpsBot: Rollout paused for deployment/eng-runtime/canary at 3629990100 per request from #eng-runtime.
Pranav: bisect final: culprit commit 7f4b2d3 - "entropy: use sample-based estimator" combined with 9a1c4ef - "kv: defer init for warm-start". Both required for the regression.
Tina: plan: revert the estimator change (7f4b2d3) in a hotfix, keep warm-start deferred commit but add the guard Hamid suggested. PRs: revert-estimator-hotfix and kv-warmstart-guard.
Alex: timeline? we can ship hotfix in ~2 hours, patch tests + canary for 30m, then unpause.
Pranav: I'll open the hotfix PR and include perf harness run in CI gating. Also adding unit test that forces selector decision on synthetic entropy.
Hamid: after hotfix, let's run extended canary with a mix of shortseq/longseq and bursty traffic to validate no regressions elsewhere.
Tina: thanks team. leaving notes in the incident tracker and linking this thread. :thumbsup:
Alex: btw, add a follow-up to evaluate the entropy estimator (sample vs streaming) with synthetic inputs; current estimator might be noisy for small token sets.
Pranav: noted, will add an evaluation notebook and metrics to the selector telemetry (entropy histogram, decisions over time).
